account.dossierIntro: Harris Teeter, Kroger's Carolinas grocery banner, runs a compact, tightly held distribution network out of two North Carolina campuses: Indian Trail near Charlotte and Greensboro. We mapped three DCs across them, holding 223 dock doors and room for about 590 trailers, with no rail at any site. Unlike most grocery yards we audit, every Harris Teeter DC sits behind a controlled truck gate, and the Indian Trail campus runs a staffed guard booth. YardFlow turns those manual gate checks into one orchestrated gate-to-dock flow across the network.
surprisingFindings: Every Harris Teeter DC sits behind a controlled truck gate, and Indian Trail runs a staffed guard booth. This is a rare grocery network that gates its yards.
Indian Trail packs both the perishable and dry-grocery DCs onto one fenced campus near Charlotte, sharing a single guarded gate and drop yard.
All three DCs run truck-only with no rail, inside two NC campuses about 90 miles apart, so the whole network is one short corridor.

fieldNotes.campusSplit: 6001 W Hwy 74 is ONE shared Harris Teeter DC campus holding a refrigerated/perishable section and a dry grocery section in a single connected mega-structure, plus a separate fleet/fuel support building near the entrance. This audit covers the PERISHABLE (refrigerated) portion: the bright white high-albedo cool-roof NW half of the main building and its NE/NW dock face and adjacent reefer drop yard. The grey-roof SE half is the dry grocery DC (covered by sister agent). Perimeter/dock/drop geofences are drawn around the perishable section only; the truck gate, access drive and guard shack are shared by the whole campus.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Controlled inner gate at the throat where the ~250m private access drive opens into the yard. Satellite z21 shows a guard booth beside the lane with a yellow barrier arm and a channelizing island; Street View pano LewhTCax-ZFpoxel2VkUmQ (2025-11) shows the gatehouse, STOP sign, pedestrian-crossing caution sign, lane markings and chain-link perimeter fencing.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Staffed booth (~1-2 vehicle footprint, multi-window) sitting beside the truck lane at the inner gate, with STOP/check-in signage. Clearly a manned guard shack, not the main building.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Gate throat opens into a very wide multi-lane paved apron with substantial unused width beside the single guarded lane; physical room to add an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large deep paved yard inside the gate before the dock doors; trucks visibly staged there in Street View.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Approach yard easily holds 3+ trucks; plus the ~250m tree-lined private drive from US-74 to the gate gives deep buffering.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Long private drive plus deep internal yard means a gate queue would not spill onto US-74; not backup-sensitive.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: ~38 doors estimated along the perishable building's NE and NW faces from z18/z19 imagery (reefer trailers backed in); band 25-50. Exact count uncertain where the perishable dock line transitions into the grocery section.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Dedicated reefer trailer drop/parking lot NE of the perishable docks; ~60 trailers visible, capacity ~90; band 25-50.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Perishable building works from a single continuous dock bank (NE/NW face); shipping and receiving not on physically separate building faces, so false. Some uncertainty given the connected grocery docks.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Indian Trail is on the southeast fringe of the Charlotte metro. Site itself is wooded edge-of-town with retention ponds and a railroad on the west edge; commercial/retail strip across US-74 to the NE and a residential subdivision to the SE. Judged Rural per rubric tie-break (small-town/edge-of-town industrial over Urban).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus: connected perishable+grocery mega-DC, a separate fleet/fuel/maintenance building near the entrance, and a third large building in the SW corner.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs along the western edge of the property but no spur visibly enters the buildings; treated as not rail-served.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale/weigh pad visible in the truck path at the gate or in the yard.
fieldNotes.coords: Pinned to the perishable building centroid (white-roof NW section), confirmed via satellite z16-z21 and Street View; the supplied campus coords (35.065177, -80.645931) landed near the shared entrance/parking area, not the perishable building.

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied coordinates (35.065177, -80.645931) landed on the campus. Wide
satellite (z15-z16) showed one large fenced industrial campus on the SW side of
W Hwy 74, bounded by a rail corridor on the SW and woods on the other sides,
with a long private access drive from the highway intersection at the NE corner.
Web research (Supermarket News, NC Commerce, AndNowUKnow) confirms this single
6001 W Hwy 74 site contains both Harris Teeter's perishable (refrigerated)
DC and its dry-grocery DC, with a ~317,000 sf dry-grocery expansion; the
complex is ~580,000 sf, serves ~104 stores across NC/SC/TN/GA/FL, and employs
360+. Positively the right building.

### Campus split (per task instruction)
The "two DCs" are not two free-standing buildings — they are joined under one
continuous stepped/L-shaped roof sharing one NE dock face and one yard:

fieldNotes.campusSplit: 6001 W Hwy 74 is ONE fenced campus holding both Harris Teeter's perishable (refrigerated) DC and its dry-grocery DC. The two are joined under one continuous stepped/L-shaped roof, not two free-standing buildings: the bright-white reflective-roof western mass reads as the older perishable/refrigerated section, the gray-roof southeastern mass is the ~317,000 sf dry-grocery expansion. This audit covers the dry-grocery (gray-roof) portion plus the shared gate, drop yard, and dock face; a sister agent covers the perishable building. Gate/yard/scale infrastructure is shared between both halves.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Confirmed in Street View (2018-11 pano rwhp4WnvSx-haTD0vStnaA): a manned guard booth with windows on multiple sides and a US flag sits in the center of the checkpoint, with a guard standing beside an inbound truck. Yellow/black barrier arms span the lanes on both sides of the booth. Also visible in z20 satellite as a small canopied structure with a truck queued at it.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Barrier-arm gates across the lanes plus chain-link perimeter fencing visible in Street View; satellite shows the access drive pinching into a controlled checkpoint at the booth.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long tree-lined private approach drive runs ~250m from the W Hwy 74 intersection (NE) down through a wooded buffer to the gate; easily stacks 3+ trucks. Street View shows a tractor-trailer climbing the drive toward the gate.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved apron immediately inside the gate (between booth and the drop yard / dock face) gives ample inside-the-fence staging before docks.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Two lanes read as inbound at the booth in Street View; exit appears single-lane. Approximate.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide multi-lane gate apron with barrier arms and unused paved width beside the booth — physical room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Very long continuous dock line along the entire NE face of the L-shaped complex (perishable + dry-grocery halves), with dozens of trailers backed in across multiple banks; combined door count well into 50+. The dry-grocery half alone is a large bank; the 50+ band reflects the shared dock face of the full complex.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Massive on-site trailer drop yard of long parallel rows holding well over 100 parked trailers (50+ band).
fieldNotes.scale: A rectangular pad near the checkpoint may be a truck scale but could not be confirmed as a weigh platform from imagery; flagged uncertain, left false.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Docks read as one continuous face serving the complex rather than two clearly separated ship/receive banks; left false, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs along the SW edge of the property (next to the long apron) but no spur appears to enter the yard / building; treated as not rail-served.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town setting on the rural fringe of Indian Trail: woods and a rail corridor on the property's south/west, light commercial along W Hwy 74 to the NE. Judged Rural per the small-town-industrial tiebreak.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: True — two large building masses (perishable + dry grocery) plus an office/maintenance cluster on one campus.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~53 acres from the perimeter polygon (the full shared fenced campus, since the yard is not separately fenced per building).

fieldNotes.truckGate: Continuous chain-link perimeter fence runs along Distribution Dr (confirmed in 2026-02 Street View). Truck drive enters through a gap with sliding/swing gate panels at the NE off Distribution Dr (~36.0954,-79.9306).
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at the truck entrance in any Street View heading; entrance is open paved drive with fence, light poles and a fire-dept standpipe only.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate present but no guard shack, so access is via kiosk/badge/call-box. Set true per rubric (gate true + guardShack false).
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved yard between buildings inside the fence provides ample inside-gate staging before docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Wide internal apron and deep yard hold well over 3 trucks between gate and docks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide gate apron and unused paved width at the Distribution Dr entrance leave room for a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock banks on opposite long faces of the main building (NE and SW), plus a separate perishable building with its own docks; medium confidence on strict ship/rcv split.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+ across the campus: long dock rows on both long faces of the main frozen/grocery building and on the perishable building to the NE. ~95 is a rough campus total.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+ parked trailers in fenced drop rows on the W/SW and N of the campus; hundreds visible.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of 3 large warehouse buildings (frozen, dry grocery, perishable) plus an office; corroborated by web research (174k sf + 50k sf perishable additions).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Dense industrial park inside the Greensboro/PTI metro fabric adjacent to Piedmont Triad International Airport.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur visible on the property.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Single combined in/out truck drive observed; lane count approximate.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Derived from the fenced perimeter polygon; approximate.
